contiguous BLAKE3 for small content ids
equal substring search in kernel and baseline
baseline graph read parses edge lists into nodes
raw bytes with a CRC-32 checked on read; fsck keeps BLAKE3
no second hash for encodings decode already verified (neutral)
zstd checksum per frame; neutral while hot content is raw
one graph is 1.4-3.7% larger than per-type stores at storage weight
dictionary cap to 1 MiB; mixed store still chose 42 KB
two clustered dictionaries; one-graph store unchanged
zlib streams in any file expanded; multiformat -38%
multiformat scored as one graph; 11-corpus score 0.57
groups up to 4 MiB; rejected by read pricing
M: shape + words contexts; cases -2.1%, multiformat -1.3%

container plans shared across re-plans; no CPU gain

codecs skipped when decode cost alone loses; identical bytes, repack CPU -25 to -90%
search each distinct chunk and seam once; score 0.43 -> 0.35, all corpora <= 1
no-dictionary plan re-planned once; identical bytes, repack CPU -10 to -25%
dissolve groups when contexts cost less; bytes-neutral, trades bytes for reads
slice/template search skipped when read work alone loses; identical output, ingest -70-98%, score 0.35 -> 0.31
graph chunks priced by reads; repo-graph 0.80 -> 0.40
trigram postings per distinct chunk; score 0.30 -> 0.26
E056 quotes do not pay under cost (transcripts slightly better without)
unused program facts cost fsck CPU; led to E097
fsck evaluates only derivations reads depend on; fsck_deep for upgrades
fastest-run timing; ingest/repack on 3 fresh stores; spread 2%
north score (one-graph bytes, archive weight 0.00097) gated beside cost; reference 0.3879; cross.rs folded in
north/tables: 24 workbooks as xlsx, csv, json, md, docx, pdf; north reference 0.3154 on three corpora
roles per north one-store; exact cross-type sharing 0 on tables and multiformat; PDF text 23% of multiformat; tables facts 13%
PDF content streams split into skeleton + UTF-8 text (via ToUnicode) as deflate-pack segment 2; multiformat 0.3344 -> 0.2953; north 0.3154 -> 0.3035; tables +0.8%

derivation records with 8-byte arg ids and builtin index; north 0.3035 -> 0.2793; cost +4.5% in timing only (instructions identical); now Repo::short_records, off by default (off byte-identical to main)
real PyPI documents and release series; kernel below the best archiver on 5 of 7 (wheels 0.36), loses on tar.gz (1.017) and vega tables vs xz (1.061); ikam CLI ingest/ls/grep/stats/serve
gzip members expanded like zlib streams; click sdists 2,149,467 -> 433,893 B (0.205 of best archiver); bench byte-identical, both scores hold
store-level encodings on all cores; identical bytes; real PDF repack 64 -> 44 s; cost score holds (counts CPU on all threads)
four pandas sdists 17.6 MB -> 3.27 MB (0.204 of xz); repack 417 s, peak 842 MiB; time in re-plans (90 of 198 s on two releases) and brotli on one 23.6 MB tar (39 s vs zstd 10 s for 3%)

each large deflate once per repack, no container re-plan of hinted contents, ranges sliced in place; pandas repack 430 -> 130 s, peak 865 -> 791 MiB, bytes identical; slow_codec_max option (82 s at 4 MiB); bench byte-identical, both scores hold

ikam live: WebDAV/watch/CLI edits as put_content + edit_tree, no repack per edit; 400 random edits 0 mismatches, p50 6-35 ms, ~1.2 KB each; live store 24% over repacked (pandas incl.); search 10.6 ms over 46 MB; bench byte-identical, both scores hold

ikam live as a service: --allow-host for a proxy name (still 127.0.0.1 only), IKAM_AUTH basic auth on every request, SIGTERM/SIGINT commit pending edits then exit; fixes edits after repacking an empty store; live bench 0 mismatches; bench exact, north 0.3035, cost 0.2510

option markup_layers (off): office XML parts as skeleton + text members per zip; north 0.3035 -> 0.3005; cases one graph -4.0% (sharing 1.0063 -> 0.9513), multiformat +1.4%, tables -0.2%; cost holds, office repack CPU up; realworld office +0.9% worst

Finder hang on Connecting: webdavfs mount sequence replayed through a Tailscale-like TLS proxy, all correct server side; --log-requests (time, method, path, host, client, status, ms; never the password or query) and UTC times on every live log line

--public (guests read-only; writes, admin, Claude answers need IKAM_AUTH), --max-body 413, --max-store 507, --max-conns 503, 431 header caps; realworld/selftest.py publishes results/latest.json; live bench 0 mismatches, fsck clean
/robots.txt: Allow on --public, Disallow otherwise (was 404), answered before the password check; for web readers that refuse the public test copy

live store grew ~5-14 KB per self-test run: a working tree per edit and files replaced before a commit, never collected; POST /api/gc and --gc-every N (off); selftest check 11 runs gc and reads every file back; ~70% of each run's bytes freed, history kept

full bench on a shallow clone panicked (divide by zero) in repo-history after minutes: its corpora come from pinned commits a shallow clone lacks; now checks each pinned commit's whole history first and exits 2 with git fetch --unshallow; scores unchanged

append-only event log (G graph of sequence labels), idempotency view and last-write-wins kv view from existing objects; April fold tests as laws; every append rebuilt the views (1,000 single appends 6.2 s); scores unchanged
graph_edit re-cuts only the chunks edits fall in (root equals put_graph); views record their log position; 1,000 single appends 6.3 to 3.1 s; objects and bytes unchanged; scores unchanged

Keys::Any for ids and kv (a real 64-bit label-key collision kept and rebuilt); graph_edit reads only its path: one edit at 10M keys 94-105 ms to 2.2-2.4 ms, upper chunks read 1,321 to 3; scores unchanged
